title: Arizona water evidence for defensible industrial growth
question: Which records show whether industrial growth has defensible water capacity?
why_it_matters: Industrial strategy in a water-constrained region depends on water rights, provider capacity, reuse, treatment, discharge, drought exposure, and public legitimacy.
current_support: FTFN has ADWR water governance and assured-supply criteria, Phoenix Water Services' April 2026 provider update, and a May 2026 Phoenix-TSMC development-agreement record defining interim wastewater conveyance improvements, accepted-flow conditions, industrial reclaimed-water-plant triggers, and customer cost responsibility.
missing_evidence: completed and accepted wastewater conveyance improvements
total facility water withdrawals and consumption
operating industrial reclaimed water plants and measured reuse
candidate_records: next City of Phoenix Water Resource Plan
executed TSMC wastewater development agreement and construction records
facility water balance, discharge, or measured reuse disclosure
next_action: Track completion and acceptance of the TSMC conveyance improvements, operation of the first industrial reclaimed water plant by June 30, 2028, and a facility water-balance or measured-reuse record before making sufficiency claims.
notes: Phase 51B added a project-specific wastewater and reclaimed-water agreement. The gap remains open because authorization and conditional flow capacity do not prove completed infrastructure, total water demand, measured reuse, drought resilience, or long-term supply sufficiency.
